clue.text: Get report after the event giving feedback about broken rib

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second here

parts.note: feed sent back, read in reverse, gives these letters

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the word rib are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from a broken rib gets a post-event report full of feedback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feedback' is read cryptically as FEED backwards, DEEF; 'about' wraps it round BRI, the anagram of RIB signalled by 'broken'.
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief someone is to question them for a report once a mission or event is over.

clue.text: Cleaner of shoes, a downtrodden type

explanation.surface: A shoe-wiper and a meek pushover.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat at the entrance for wiping feet, and figuratively a person others walk over.

clue.text: Stop falling behind, exhausted

parts.note: bottom means the backside
out means used up, finished

explanation.surface: Someone tired, trailing at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices bottom out when they reach their lowest point and stop declining.

clue.text: I put out diamonds etc for model

parts.note: to deal is to hand out cards, diamonds and other suits

explanation.surface: Someone sets out jewellery as a fashion display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds etc' suggests gems but means card suits, dealt out.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example to be imitated.

clue.text: Perhaps the sole defender in port

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish, an example of a fish
a guard defends

explanation.surface: The only protector stationed in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' reads as 'only' but is the flatfish; FISHGUARD is a ferry port in Pembrokeshire, west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishguard is a Welsh harbour town with ferries to Ireland.

clue.text: Loud behaviour shows dissension in group

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud
action means conduct or behaviour

explanation.surface: Rowdy conduct reveals a split within a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Faction can mean party strife, internal discord within a political body.

clue.text: Best maiden

explanation.surface: A top unmarried girl.
explanation.definitionFit: First means top-ranked, and a maiden voyage or speech is the initial one.

clue.text: Doctor can change pact

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the clue words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician can alter an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges all nine letters of DOCTOR and CAN; 'Doctor' looks like the verb or the anagram signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Hard to support flag of a republic

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece is written beneath the other

parts.note: the yellow flag is a kind of iris
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Patriotic instruction to hold up a nation's banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the iris plant; H sits below it, 'to support' in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to Ireland, whose state is officially a republic.

clue.text: Armed gangster turns up and seizes gold pieces

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gun is slang for a gunman
gets means grabs or obtains

explanation.surface: A gunman arrives and grabs the gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses GUN to NUG ahead of GETS; it looks like 'arrives'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuggets are lumps of precious metal found in the ground.

clue.text: True love can be so unconventional

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A romantic remark that genuine love may be unorthodox.
explanation.walkthrough: O (love, nil in tennis scoring) comes first, then 'can be' rearranges TRUE to UTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré is a borrowed French word for eccentric, beyond the bounds of propriety.

clue.text: Flat out in the short run

explanation.surface: Exhausted and lying down, at least for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat out' looks like collapsed and 'in the short run' like 'for now', but both are racing terms: full speed, and taking part in a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Going at top speed, and also running a brief race, both describe a dash on the track.

clue.text: Do extra work to make satellite touch down

parts.note: the Moon is Earth's natural satellite
to light is to land or alight, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: Instructions for landing a spacecraft, oddly cast as overtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonlighting is holding a second job on the side, often at night.

clue.text: Irishman's exclamation about Orange type

parts.note: och is an exclamation used in Ireland and Scotland
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An Irishman exclaims over a kind of Orangeman, hinting at Ulster politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orange' suggests the Orange Order of Northern Ireland, fitting the Irish surface, but it is just a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment of yellowish-orange hue.

clue.text: Fish it takes five people to play

definitions.text: it takes five people to play

explanation.surface: A fishing trip where the whole team is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Schubert's Trout Quintet is a famous piece for five players, hence the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater game fish, and Schubert's quintet nicknamed after his song about one.

clue.text: Score just exceeded in game

parts.note: a score is twenty, and going one beyond it names a card game where the target is that total

explanation.surface: A match where the final tally narrowly passed a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty; one more gives the card game also called pontoon or blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game in which players aim for a total of cards just past a score without going over.

clue.text: Cunning with fists shown by nobles

parts.note: arch means sly or knowingly mischievous
dukes is slang for fists, as in 'put up your dukes'

explanation.surface: Aristocrats showing shrewdness and readiness to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Archdukes were princes of high rank, notably in the Habsburg house of Austria.

clue.text: Whip catching MP hard cheese? No

indicators.note: catching means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: cat, the cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A party whip nabbing a politician gets tough luck, or does he?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' and 'MP' suggest Parliament's party enforcers; 'hard cheese' is British slang for bad luck, but the 'No' says this cheese is soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft French cheese, the opposite of a hard one.

clue.text: Not dismissing charge before performing

parts.note: keeping means custody or care, as in a child in one's charge
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: An employer retaining staff responsible for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping on an employee means retaining them rather than sacking them.

clue.text: Villain gets mother a large port

parts.note: a rotter is a cad or scoundrel
dam is a mother, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A scoundrel collects his mother from the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch city stands among Europe's biggest seaports.

clue.text: Character in Ivanhoe or another novel

explanation.surface: A literary choice between Scott and something else.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jewish heroine of Scott's Ivanhoe, and Daphne du Maurier's novel titled with the same name.

clue.text: Take steps to shift direction of trade

indicators.note: to shift tells us a letter in the word trade moves to a new position

parts.note: E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A call to act and change how commerce is heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shift' moves the E (east, a direction) of TRADE forward to sit after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to walk, putting one foot after the other.

clue.text: Depart for some work up in Norfolk town

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: an erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Someone leaves to take a job in rural East Anglia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ERG (a unit of work) to GRE, and 'in' puts it inside DISS, a small town in the English county of Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to depart from the main subject.

clue.text: Persistently harass enemy leader into defeat

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to best someone is to beat them

indicators.note: leader indicates the first letter of the word enemy

explanation.surface: Military advice: keep pestering, and push the foe's commander toward collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives E, and 'into' puts it inside BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Beset means to attack or trouble on all sides, without letting up.

clue.text: Producing sound in unison? I conduct

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A choirmaster asks whether everyone is singing together under his baton.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic means relating to or making audible waves.

clue.text: Thwart poor players somewhere in Herts

parts.note: hams are bad, overacting performers
Tring is a town in Hertfordshire

explanation.surface: Bad actors performing at some Hertfordshire venue are hindered.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is Hertfordshire, a county north of London; TRING is a small market town there.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamstring is to cripple, so to frustrate or hinder someone's plans.

clue.text: Worry third member of undistinguished trio

explanation.surface: Concern about the last of three nobodies.
explanation.walkthrough: Every Tom, Dick and Harry means just anybody, so the third of the trio is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to pester or harass, and the name ends the phrase for ordinary people.

clue.text: Trail dog

explanation.surface: Following a hound's path.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is a path or trail, and to dog someone is to follow or track them.

clue.text: Coming together to study series of lessons

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a course is a set of classes

explanation.surface: Students gathering for a programme of classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a gathering or confluence, a flowing together of people or things.

clue.text: Reason for quarrel

explanation.surface: Grounds for a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to make a reasoned case, and also to dispute or row.

clue.text: Tell-tale describes skill in this

parts.note: a 'tell-tale' seems a sneak, but it is the story of William Tell, who shot an apple off his son's head with a crossbow

explanation.surface: A sneak's account boasts of someone's talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell-tale' looks like a gossip; it is the legend of William Tell, the Swiss marksman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tell legend celebrates prowess at shooting with bow and bolt.

clue.text: Money made thanks to high cards

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
kings rank among the top cards in a pack

explanation.surface: Winnings earned through holding top cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the receipts or revenue a business brings in.
